questions.def: Use the simple past for completed actions in the past.
questions.question: They ___ to the cinema last night.

questions.def: Use simple past for a completed action at a specific time.
questions.question: She ___ her keys this morning.

questions.def: After 'didn't', use the base form of the verb.
questions.question: He didn't saw the accident yesterday.

questions.def: Simple past for a completed period of time in the past.
questions.question: I ___ in London for five years.

questions.def: Use past continuous for an action in progress when another interrupted it.
questions.question: We ___ TV when the phone rang.

questions.def: Use 'was' to report what he said in the past.
questions.question: He said he ___ tired.

questions.def: 'Last year' requires the simple past, not present perfect.
questions.question: They have visited Rome last year.

questions.def: Use past perfect for an action completed before another in the past.
questions.question: She ___ at the company before she moved.

questions.def: Use past perfect for an action completed before a specific time.
questions.question: I ___ never ___ sushi before last week.

questions.def: Use past perfect for an action completed before another in the past.
questions.question: By the time we arrived, the movie ___.

questions.def: 'Yesterday' requires simple past; 'is gone' is present perfect.
questions.question: She is gone to Italy yesterday.

questions.def: Use the past tense 'were' for the plural subject 'they'.
questions.question: They ___ tired after the long journey.

questions.def: Use past continuous for simultaneous actions in the past.
questions.question: While he ___, she was reading a book.

questions.def: Simple past for a completed action.
questions.question: She ___ to the party, but she didn't want to.

questions.def: 'Yesterday' requires simple past; 'am seeing' is present continuous.
questions.question: I am seeing him yesterday evening.

questions.def: Use past perfect to show an action completed before another.
questions.question: We ___ dinner before they arrived.

questions.def: Use past perfect for an action that finished before another.
questions.question: He ___ the letter before he left.

questions.def: Past perfect requires 'had' + past participle.
questions.question: By the time I woke up, she ___ already gone.

questions.def: 'Since' requires present perfect continuous, not present continuous.
questions.question: She is working here since 2015.

questions.def: Use simple past for a completed action at a specific time.
questions.question: I ___ her last summer.

questions.def: Past continuous for an action in progress at a specific time.
questions.question: What ___ you ___ at 8 PM last night?

questions.def: Use the simple past for completed actions in the past.
questions.question: He ___ the game yesterday.

questions.def: 'Yesterday' indicates a completed action, so use simple past.
questions.question: They are leaving already yesterday.

questions.def: Use simple past for actions completed in the past.
questions.question: I ___ him at the park yesterday.

questions.def: Use 'was' to describe a state in the past.
questions.question: She ___ happy when she heard the news.

questions.def: Past perfect describes action finished before another in past.
questions.question: Before she went to bed, she ___ her teeth.

questions.def: 'Last week' requires simple past, not present perfect.
questions.question: He has gone to the store last week.

questions.def: Use simple past to ask about completed actions in the past.
questions.question: What ___ you ___ last weekend?

questions.def: Past continuous uses 'were' for the plural subject 'they'.
questions.question: They ___ playing when it started to rain.

questions.def: Simple past is needed for a completed action in the past.
questions.question: She ___ to the concert yesterday.
